entries.odia: ପରଧନେ ଲହର ଫହର; ଛଡାଇ ନେଲେ ଲାଜେ ମର
entries.title: A flourish on someone else’s wealth
entries.literal_meaning: You move about in style on another’s wealth; when it is taken away, you die of shame.
entries.explanation: The first half gives someone room to move and make a show; the second suddenly takes that support away. The dictionary defines the headword as moving to and fro, while the verse puts that movement on another person’s wealth. Read as a taunt, it catches the embarrassment of displaying what one cannot claim as one’s own. The closing “die of shame” is exaggerated reproach, not a literal instruction. Our wider reading concerns borrowed display and insecure pretension, not the worth of people who receive help.
entries.meaning_odia: ପରର ଧନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଲହର ଫହର; ସେ ଧନ ଫେରିଗଲେ ଦେଖାଣିର ଭିତ୍ତିଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହେନାହିଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଭାଗର ଆରାମ ଓ ଚଳପ୍ରଚଳକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଭାଗର ଲାଜ ହଠାତ୍ ଅଟକାଇଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜର ନୁହେଁ ଏମିତି ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ଏହି ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ। “ଲାଜେ ମର” କଥାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ; ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Borrowed display can become embarrassment when its support is withdrawn.
entries.odia_summary: ପରର ଧନରେ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣ ଦେଖାଇଲେ, ତାହା ଫେରିଗଲେ ଲାଜରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଟାହି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone poses with a friend’s expensive camera and lets others think it belongs to them. When the friend asks for it back, another friend quotes the saying softly. The joke concerns the false impression, not borrowing a camera.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; this is a source label, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The display reading is editorial close reading, not an independently supplied traditional-use gloss.

entries.odia: ଦଦରା ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗା, ମଝି ନଈରେ ଦେଲୁ ଦଗା
entries.title: The boat fails midstream
entries.literal_meaning: Worn-out boat, you betrayed me in the middle of the river.
entries.explanation: The boat is addressed as though it had broken a promise. Its failure comes in midstream, where the traveller is already relying on it and cannot simply step back onto the bank. That timing gives the short complaint its force. As an editorial application, it can describe an unreliable tool or arrangement failing at the moment it is most needed. The line supplies a vivid reproach; it does not establish a real accident or give instructions for crossing a river.
entries.meaning_odia: ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗାକୁ ମଣିଷ ପରି ଡାକି କୁହାଯାଉଛି—ତୁ ଠିକ୍ ମଝି ନଈରେ ଦଗା ଦେଲୁ। କୂଳରେ ଥିଲେ ପଛକୁ ଫେରିହେବ; ମଝିରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲା ପରେ ସେହି ଭରସା ଭାଙ୍ଗିବାର କଷ୍ଟ ଅଧିକ। ଦଦରା ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗା ଓ ଦଗାର ଧ୍ୱନିମିଳ ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ଆହୁରି ମନେ ରଖାଏ। ଆମର ଆଧୁନିକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ, ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ଅଚଳ ହୋଇଯାଉଥିବା ଉପକରଣ ବା ଭରସାହୀନ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: A sharp complaint about support that fails after one has already depended on it.
entries.odia_summary: ଭରସା କରି ଆଗେଇଯିବା ପରେ ଠିକ୍ ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ସେହି ଭରସା ଭାଙ୍ଗିବାର ଅଭିଯୋଗ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Halfway through a presentation, an unreliable projector stops working. The presenter smiles ruefully and quotes the boat line while opening a printed copy. The comparison is to badly timed equipment failure, not to an actual river incident.
entries.cultural_context: The source defines the river’s middle and supplies the labelled quotation; it does not narrate an accident or identify a speaker. The figurative equipment example is original editorial application. The page carries a need-check category; no silent textual correction is proposed.

entries.odia: ଷାଠିଏ କାହାଣ ତଣ୍ଡକୁ ଅଛି, ହରି ଭଗତିକି କଡ଼ାଏ ନାହିଁ
entries.title: Plenty for penalties, nothing for devotion
entries.literal_meaning: There are sixty kahans for penalties, but not a small cowrie amount for devotion to Hari.
entries.explanation: The verse sets a large expense beside a tiny amount refused. Its religious contrast is explicit: money can be found for a penalty or an expense one is forced to bear, yet none is available for devotion to Hari. The dictionary’s separate definition of taṇḍa includes fines and compelled expenditure; it does not tell us what offence, if any, lies behind this line. Our reading hears a reproach about priorities, made memorable by the unequal sums. That reading preserves the devotional voice without making spending on worship a test of anyone’s goodness.
entries.meaning_odia: ତଣ୍ଡ ପାଇଁ ବଡ଼ ଅଙ୍କର ଧନ ଅଛି, ହରିଙ୍କ ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅସମାନ ତୁଳନାରେ କଥାର ଖୋଚା। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ତଣ୍ଡର ଅର୍ଥ ଜୋରିମାନାଠାରୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଅଛି; ଏଠାରେ କେଉଁ ଘଟଣାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କେଉଁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଟଙ୍କା ମିଳେ ଓ କେଉଁ କାମ ବେଳେ ଅଭାବ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ସେହି ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହା ପଚାରେ। ମୂଳ କଥାର ଭକ୍ତିଭାବ ରହିଥାଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପୂଜାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାକୁ ମଣିଷର ଭଲମନ୍ଦର ମାପ କରିବା ଆମର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A devotional reproach contrasts large compelled expenses with a small amount withheld.
entries.odia_summary: ବାଧ୍ୟ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପାଇଁ ବହୁତ, ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଚା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends discuss someone who readily pays repeated late fees but says there is nothing to spare for a small devotional gathering they had promised to support. One quotes the line as a comment on those priorities. The scene is invented and is not a demand that anyone fund religious activity.
entries.cultural_context: The primary headword explains a large sum in an older cowrie vocabulary. The lexical taṇḍa source is context-only, not a second witness of the saying. No exact modern currency conversion, offence, historic event or duty to donate is asserted.

entries.odia: ମୁଁ ଖାଇ ନାହିଁ, ପାଟି ଖାଇଚି ନିୟାମ କରିବା ଆସ
entries.title: The mouth ate, not I
entries.literal_meaning: I have not eaten; my mouth has eaten. Come, let us take an oath.
entries.explanation: The speaker tries to separate the mouth from the person who used it. The invitation to swear then gives this flimsy distinction an exaggerated air of certainty. Read as a joke about evasion, the line exposes how changing the subject of a sentence can leave the action unchanged. The dictionary explains taking an oath and records the saying; the account of evasive reasoning is our close reading. Its comic force lies in the transparent excuse, not in proving that every denial is dishonest.
entries.meaning_odia: ଖାଇଛି ପାଟି, ମୁଁ ନୁହେଁ—ନିଜ ଅଙ୍ଗକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦାୟ ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ ଯୁକ୍ତି। ତାହା ପରେ ନିୟାମ କରିବାକୁ ଡାକିବାରେ ସେହି ଦୁର୍ବଳ ସଫେଇ ଆହୁରି ହାସ୍ୟକର ହୁଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କଥାର କର୍ତ୍ତା ବଦଳାଇଦେଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମଟି ବଦଳେନାହିଁ—ଏହା ସେହି ଫାଙ୍କିକୁ ଧରେ। ଯେଉଁଠି ସଫେଇଟି ନିଜେ ନିଜର ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ଦେଖାଇଦେଉଛି, ସେଠି ଏହି ରସ ଲାଗେ; ସବୁ ଅସ୍ୱୀକାରକୁ ମିଛ ଭାବିବାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: An absurd division between a person and their mouth makes an evasive excuse visible.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜ କାମର ଦାୟ ପାଟି ଉପରେ ପକାଇ ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ହାସ୍ୟକର ସଫେଇ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend finishes the last biscuit and jokingly claims that only their mouth ate it. Another answers with the full saying, including the invitation to swear. Both know what happened, so the exchange makes fun of the excuse rather than staging an accusation.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels niyāma karibā a rural verb for swearing an oath. That register label is not evidence of rural dishonesty. No specific oath ritual, legal validity or origin story is supplied.
